title: Introduce CI Harmonizer, targeted cache warmup, and dependency-freshness probe
author: Eleanor Chen
release_notes: Adds a CI harmonizer composite action to centralize presubmit configuration, a lightweight cache-warm tool to reduce cold-cache presubmit latency, and a dependency-freshness probe that gates merges on stale transitive deps. No runtime behavior changes to production code. Upgrade notes included.
summary: Converge presubmit configuration into a reusable CI Harmonizer, add targeted cache warmup and a dependency freshness probe to reduce flakiness and surface stale deps earlier.
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit workflows had diverged across services (multiple workflow fragments, ad-hoc cache keys, and duplicated runner settings). This made cache warmups ineffective, increased cold-starts for CI, and caused several flakes due to stale transitive dependencies. This PR introduces a lightweight, incremental approach: 1) CI Harmonizer composite action that centralizes common runner settings and lint/test invocation patterns; 2) targeted cache-warm tool that primes layer-level caches only for changed modules (reduces warmup scope and time); 3) dependency-freshness probe that runs a fast transitive-dep check and fails the presubmit with clear remediation hints when deps are stale.

What this PR changes (high level): - Adds .github/actions/ci-harmonizer (composite action) and migrates presubmit workflows to use the harmonizer instead of duplicating lists of steps. - Adds tools/ci/cache_warm.go: small Go binary used by the harmonizer to warm relevant caches in parallel (s3/remote-cache or local action cache depending on runner). - Adds tools/ci/dep_probe.go: fast transitive-dep freshness probe used as an early gate; returns non-zero with a diagnostic artifact when it finds outdated transitive locks. - Introduces a lightweight presubmit workflow template .github/workflows/presubmit-harmonized.yml which uses the harmonizer and exposes parameters for shard profiles and fast-vs-full lanes. - Minor updates to docs and ci/README.md describing migration steps and how to opt out for special cases.

Checklist:
- [x] Central composite action implemented and unit-tested locally
- [x] Cache warm tool implemented and smoke-tested in a dedicated job
- [x] Dependency probe implemented with clear actionable output
- [x] Migrated 8 core service workflows to harmonized template
- [x] Backwards-compatible: per-repo overrides remain possible via input flags
- [x] Metrics hooks added to console (CI latency, cache-hit trend)

Commits summary: "Initial commit: ci-harmonizer composite action and template"; "add cache_warm tool + docs"; "add dep_probe and wire into presubmit template"; "migrate services: redwood, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-docs"; "fix lint + update go.mod and add smoke tests".

Files changed (high level): [.github/actions/ci-harmonizer/action.yml, .github/workflows/presubmit-harmonized.yml, .github/workflows/presubmit-redwood.yml (migrated), tools/ci/cache_warm.go, tools/ci/dep_probe.go, tools/ci/Makefile, ci/README.md, docs/internal/ci-migration.md, scripts/ci-wrap.sh, go.mod, go.sum, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ci-change.md]

Testing and validation performed: - Ran harmonized presubmit against redwood monorepo with sample change sets; observed median presubmit latency down ~18% for cold-cache jobs and warmup CPU usage limited to targeted modules. - Ran dep_probe across a subset of repos and validated diagnostic output on known stale transitive-dep scenarios. - Ran end-to-end presubmit on a staging runner; initial run showed a lint failure due to a strict rule (fixed in follow-up commit). All CI checks green after fixes. - Verified that existing explicit workflow overrides still work by adding an example to ci/README.md.

Migration notes for service owners: - To opt into the harmonized presubmit, replace your presubmit workflow with the presubmit-harmonized.yml template or call the composite action directly. - If you rely on custom pre-step behavior, provide inputs to the composite to run hooks; see docs/internal/ci-migration.md for examples. - If you cannot adopt immediately, the previous workflows remain available for 2 weeks; automation will open follow-up PRs to migrate remaining services.

Observability and rollout plan: - Console: new CI metrics (presubmit median latency, cache-warm hit-rate) are emitted as tags "ci.harmonizer" and available under the CI dashboard. - Gradual rollout: migrated 8 high-traffic services in first wave, monitor for 72 hours, then bulk migrate remaining repos in the monorepo. - Rollback: revert to the previous workflow files (kept as .github/workflows/presubmit-legacy/*.yml) and disable dep_probe by setting input allow_dep_probe=true.

Why this is different from previous CI refactors: Instead of a large, opinionated monolith, the harmonizer is a small composite action that centralizes runner config while allowing per-repo overrides and pluggable probe/warmup binaries. The dep_probe focuses on transitive-dep freshness rather than full lockfile substitution, reducing noise and improving signal-to-noise for developers.
commits: 4 commits: 1) add ci-harmonizer composite + template (action.yml + workflow template) 2) add cache_warm tool + Makefile + docs 3) add dep_probe + presubmit wiring + smoke job 4) fixes: lint, tests, migration examples

2026-03-03 - Connor Lee: dep_probe output is useful, but the diagnostic artifact can be large. Can we limit to top 10 offenders and provide a link to full log?
2026-03-03 - Eleanor Chen: Implemented summary output (top 10) plus artifact upload link to the full probe log. Updated docs with example output.

2026-03-04 - Ravi Patel: lgtm for the composite. One nit: prefer inputs.named 'shard_profile' to accept 'fast,balanced,full' rather than numeric shard counts. Also add a flag to override container image for hermetic builds.
2026-03-04 - Eleanor Chen: Updated action inputs to accept 'shard_profile' enum and added 'override_runner_image' input. Added migration note in docs.
